# Tupac Estate Demands Drake Remove 'Taylor Made Freestyle' Over AI Voice (Rolling Stone)

By Jon Blistein. Published April 24, 2024.

## Key findings
- The **Tupac Shakur estate** sent **Drake** a **cease-and-desist letter** demanding he take down his Kendrick Lamar diss, **"Taylor Made Freestyle,"** because it allegedly used an **unauthorized AI-generated version of Tupac's voice.**
- The letter, sent by lawyer **Howard King** and obtained by Rolling Stone, called the use a "flagrant violation of Tupac's publicity and the estate's legal rights" and a "blatant abuse of the legacy of one of the greatest hip-hop artists of all time."
- King gave Drake 24 hours to take down the track or face legal action. (News first reported by Billboard.)
- "Taylor Made Freestyle" appeared to feature **AI vocals from Tupac and an AI-generated Snoop Dogg.**
- Drake did **not** officially release the song on streaming services (where it would earn royalties) — only as a video on social media.
- King said the song had "generated well more than one million streams" and been "widely reported in the general national press."
- The letter referenced the viral AI-generated song "Heart on My Sleeve" (voice clones of Drake and the Weeknd) and Drake's own efforts to clamp down on unauthorized uses of his likeness.

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — Rolling Stone, top-tier; obtained the cease-and-desist letter.
- Establishes: Drake used AI-generated vocals of Tupac (and Snoop Dogg) in "Taylor Made Freestyle" (Apr 2024, Kendrick beef); Tupac estate issued cease-and-desist; track not officially released to streaming; 1M+ streams as a social video. This is a human artist (Drake) using AI in a released (social) hip-hop track.
